ITEM 1 mechanism, all read: ase::ui::optsheet_fill (src/ase_window.tcl) ends in ase::ui::optsheet_preview; that proc is the ONLY caller of ase::opt_preview in src/ and passes `{}` as plan and ase::ui::optsheet_netlist_text's answer as the fourth argument; optsheet_netlist_text reads <rundir>/<cell>.spice whole into a local, keeps dot cards with `+` continuations and `.control`..`.endc`, and caches only the reduced text per file by {size mtime} in ase::ui::optsheet_nlcache; it never calls ase::rundir.

ase::opt_preview (src/ase.tcl) uses netlist_text only for ase::run_seed_line; `control` entries are {option-name line}; the suppression loop walks the state's rows first, then ase::preview_analysis_types; notes are a dict keyed by option name; the leak sentence is composed there from ase::opt_leak_why. The pane prints `[lindex $e 1]` only, and notes under `not delivered` as `<name> — <why>`: there is no analysis label anywhere, so the comment 'each line tagged with the analysis it belongs to' is false as built.

ase::preview_analysis_types calls `ase::analysis_emit_order $state 0 $sim` and falls back to row order on a raise; its only caller is ase::opt_preview; the DECLARED LIMIT comment naming issue 1657 stands above it.

render_deck (ase::backend::ngspice): `op_last` is 1 iff optier_ctl or optier_post is non-empty; they are filled only under ase::op_gate_on + ase::op_analysis_enabled + a non-empty ase::op_cards_for, by tier: a -> optier_ctl, d -> optier_post, b -> optier_write only, default -> optier_ctl only when ase::n_enabled_analyses > 1. A miss takes the `elseif {![ase::op_cards_hit ...]}` arm: no cards, op first. Scope pre, suppress pre, ..., suppress post, scope post are written per ROW; a design-variable dc row takes dcvar_body before those lines.

ase::op_save_tier: tier b is reachable only through ase::op_tier_force_set (the capability ladder answers c, d or a), and a forced b with more devices than ase::op_write_max_names is demoted to c. op_save_tier/op_tier_now can start the simulator on a capability-cache miss (their own headers); ase::op_tier_forced is a plain variable read.

The op_cards slot is one process-wide dict {netlist block}; ase::op_cards_hit is exact string equality; ase::op_cards_capture clears first, reads the netlist with `open r`/`read` (the same default translation the window's reader and ase::run_deck use), and with the gate off returns after the clear with no record. op_annot::_block answers {} or `.save all` plus at least one card, which settles most of the scout's third unverified item.
ase::saves_op_cards_coming spells gate + op enabled + held block and is called by render_deck for its leader.

ITEM 2 mechanism, all read: read_dataset() (src/save.c) on a typeless call sets type `op` at an `Integrated Noise` first plot and stores it as `op` (integ_is_op stays 1 when op_asked is 0); extra_rawfile() what==1 spice arm switches with no read on a (rawfile, sim_type) hit, and on the path alone when type is NULL; the non-spice arm has its own copy of the loop; the clear arm sets extra_idx and extra_prev_idx to 0.

The annotate_op arm (src/scheduler.c) deletes (xctx->raw->rawfile, xctx->raw->sim_type) only when the CURRENT database is a one-point op/dc, then asks extra_rawfile(1, f, "op"), then "dc", then "tran". `xschem raw_read` clears the whole registry and calls read_rawfile_by_type() directly, so Raw.req_sim_type stays NULL on that door for a typed read too; raw_case_reread() re-reads with req_sim_type.

wrong.claim: Rows A64-2 and O29b of test_op_annot slice the annotate_op arm's C source.
wrong.correction: Only A64-2 does. O29b slices annot_overlay_sync() in src/actions.c. A64-2 needs `extra_rawfile` and `update_op` to stay on code lines of the arm and `live_cursor2_backannotate` to stay off them; its slice ends at the first line that is exactly the arm's own indent plus `}`.

wrong.claim: The annotate_op arm makes three plain calls into the dedupe arm (op, dc, tran).
wrong.correction: Four shapes: with a fifth word (`xschem annotate_op <file> <level> <sim_type>`) it makes ONE call with that type and no fallback. Option 2A has to say whether the widened drop applies there.
wrong.evidence: annotate_op arm, src/scheduler.c: `if(sim_type[0]) { res = extra_rawfile(1, f, sim_type, ...); } else { ...op, dc, tran... }`.

wrong.claim: 2B's mark is set in the integrated-noise arm 'for a caller that did NOT ask for op and no dataset has been taken yet (`!op_asked`, raw->datasets == 0)'.
wrong.correction: `!op_asked` is not 'typeless': the function overwrites `type`, so a new local taken on entry (type == NULL) is needed. And `datasets == 0` leaves one case out: on a typeless read with the operating point FIRST the same arm still answers `op` (integ_is_op is 1), so totals with as many variables as the operating point are appended as a second `op` dataset and that database is also 'shown as it stands' to a later request for op. Mark on 'this typeless read took an Integrated Noise plot as op', whichever dataset it was. No fixture of band M has equal variable counts (IN has 2 names, OP has 3), so this is read, not measured.
wrong.evidence: read_dataset(): `if(!type) type = "op"; ... if(!strcmp(type, "op")) { if(integ_is_op) sim_type = "op"; else integ_held = 1; }` and the comment's DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED item 'a read that names no type takes the first plot ... and every later one of that plot's type, this one included, in every order'; m_plots in tests/headless/test_raw_ascii_point_bounds.tcl.

wrong.claim: Acceptance row 'M-loaded' runs on in_nsd_op, in_nsd_op_op2, in_op_nsd_op2, inc_nsd_op, inq_nsq_op, in_nsd_opm, ins_nsd_op.
wrong.correction: ins_nsd_op is vacuous: its typeless cell is `refused(0)`, so no totals database is left for the second read to meet. in_nsd_opm is not vacuous but its re-read answer is stored as `dc` (multi-point promotion), so the entry's registry key changes from (f, op) to (f, dc) and a later `raw read f op` reads again and appends. The row needs a premise leg per file: the typeless read answered 1 and its first name is v(onoise_total).
wrong.evidence: m_want: `ins_nsd_op - same {refused(0) ...}`; `in_nsd_opm op rule {dc ds=1 pts=3 ...}` and `in_nsd_opm - same {op ds=1 pts=1 ... v(onoise_total) ...}`.

WITH CHANGES, both items. The rulings stay the user's.

ITEM 1 -- C holds as the direction; four things in the sketch break as written. (1) The op-last answer has to belong to the backend that applies it: a core predicate would order the pane by ngspice's rule for every backend (HK3 drives a hookless one; the adapter spec's section 7.2 says the order is the adapter's). Make it an optional hook, or gate it, and move that spec section either way. (2) 'The true order when it can be known' is true only at the moment of the last repaint: the sheet is non-modal and nothing repaints it on a netlist, a gate change or an analysis edit. Add the repaint or state the limit. (3) The pane code has diverged in the private tree (pure text proc, inline default note, another reader); write the pane text as a pure proc here too and plan the merge, which also moves the label row to the counted arm. (4) The window can read a different file from the run's (local_netlist_dir), so UNKNOWN must cover 'no file found where the run will look'. Smaller: new argument fifth, keep the unreduced text away from ase::run_seed_line, fix the suppression loop's name-by-line product rather than copying it, give a label a shape that cannot be read as a deck line. The leak sentence should not be reworded until the dcvar `reset` question is measured.

ITEM 2 -- B does not hold as sketched. It is reached from a draw (graph walkers with autoload=true, restoring by index), from calc::aq_restore (a restore that would become a re-read), and from raw_select(), where the spec forbids clearing or freeing and where a select with no type is turned into a request for `op`. If B is ruled, it must replace in the same slot, read first and replace on success, be opt-in per caller (the annotate arm would need the bit too), and set its mark on 'a typeless read took an Integrated Noise plot as op' rather than on the first dataset. Even then it leaves the publishers that never read: `raw switch`, `raw switch_back`, the cadence chord's first two rungs, calc::aq_run in place. A holds as issue 0685's engine fix under its section 4 (row F12 moves, the explicit-type call shape needs a decision) and is the smaller, better-bounded change; by itself it leaves `raw read <f> op` and `raw select` showing the totals. The option the scout only asks about -- a typeless read not storing the totals as `op` when the file holds an operating point -- is the one that reaches every reader, and it has no map and moves `same` cells of band M; put it on the table with a map or drop the question. C (leave, documented) is unchanged by this review.
